answers.assumption_check: Load-bearing: the bus can start and carry 'database start' while the database is refused, because the bus opens its table lazily (bus.py:333) and DatabaseProxyDevice wakes without touching the store; read 2026-11-18. A refusal inside the bus process itself would send the wake back to that same process and time out loudly rather than hang silently.
answers.builder_check: A Haiku builder needs: psycopg2.OperationalError's text for a refusal contains 'Connection refused' (Linux) or 'actively refused' / 'could not connect' with 10061 (Windows), so _refused matches 'refused' case-folded; _conn_args() returns {'host': sockdir} for a socket dial and host/port/passfile for TCP; the bus target string is module:Class; RemoteBus().verbs returns a dict with 'exit' and 'text'; the proof must never dial a real port, so it monkeypatches store.psycopg2.connect, store._wake_proxy and time.sleep.

answers.falsifier_check: Proof cairn/devices/db_domain/tools/client/proofs/test_a_refused_dial_wakes_the_database_proxy.py, one tooth per clause: (1) a refused TCP loopback dial wakes the proxy exactly once and the dial is retried until it connects; (2) a socket dial that fails, and a TCP failure that is not a refusal, raise at once and never wake; (3) a wake that fails, or a refusal still standing after the retry window, raises the refusal naming why; (4) the wake asks the bus for start on cairn.devices.dbproxy.shim:DatabaseProxyShim, a class that exists, and store.py imports nothing from cairn.devices.dbproxy. Red first, green twice. Horizon: this build.
